{{Quote|He's a master codebreaker, an ace pilot, a poet with a blaster.|Maz Kanata to Finn, Rose, and [[Poe Dameron]]|<ref name="Episode VIII" />}}
The '''Master Codebreaker''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] codebreaker who had an association with the [[Pirate Queen]] [[Maz Kanata]] and a love for gambling.

==Biography==
===Tomorrow never dies===
{{Quote|Perfecting the arts of infiltration, espionage, and high-stakes bluffing requires that I rub extremities with the most valuable players in the galaxy.|Master Codebreaker, in the ''Smuggler's Guide''|<ref name="Smuggler's Guide">''[[Star Wars: Smuggler's Guide]]''</ref>}}
Sometime after [[Supreme Leader]] [[Snoke]]'s assumption of leadership within the [[First Order]], Master Codebreaker stole the ''[[Smuggler's Guide]]'' from the [[Kanjiklub]] [[Unidentified Kanjiklub chief|chief]] in the middle of negotiations for the domination of Rim territories, and wondered if [[Maz Kanata]] intended the [[book]] for him as another one of their tests of intellect. Before trying to uncover the enigma, Codebreaker visited the betting parlors of [[Cardota|Hosnian Cardota]], where he played with the [[arms dealer]]s, steadily decreasing their money supply to their offense. Eventually, one of them tried to [[poison]] him, but the toxicity was nullified by [[Hullepi/Canon|hullepi]]-culture [[tongue sheath]]. He claimed to exit the parlor from the 350th-floor balcony using a [[Para-wing glider/Canon|para-wing glider]]. Master Codebreaker then returned to the enigma of the logbook and wrote an entry detailing this exploit in the ''Smuggler's Guide''.<ref name="Smuggler's Guide" />

===Top-flight arms dealers and syndicates===
{{Quote|Furthermore, my experience in the Hosnian system made me realize that you neglected to credit the galaxy's true powers—perhaps by design?|Master Codebreaker, in the ''Smuggler's Guide''|<ref name="Smuggler's Guide" />}}
Following his experience in the [[Hosnian system]], Codebreaker noticed that Maz's list of powerful [[Five Crime Syndicates|crime syndicates]] was [[Standard decade|decades]] out of date and that she neglected to mention [[the galaxy]]'s true powers. He then wrote in the ''Smuggler's Guide'' new list of powerful syndicates: [[Black Sun]] lost their place in the list; the [[Crymorah Syndicate]] was replaced by [[Droid Gotra]]; [[Crimson Dawn]] was replaced by [[Son-tuul Pride]] and the [[Guavian Death Gang]]; the [[Pyke]]s and [[Hutt]]s were replaced by [[Kanjiklub]] and the [[Red Key Raiders]]. He also added corporate entities that Maz neglected to mention: [[Sienar Fleet Systems]], [[BlasTech Industries|BlasTech]], [[Kuat Drive Yards]], [[Mining Guild]], and [[Corporate Sector Authority]].<ref name="Smuggler's Guide" />

===Cipher machine===
{{Quote|I am reminded that very little ever really changes.|Master Codebreaker, in the ''Smuggler's Guide''|<ref name="Smuggler's Guide" />}}
Taking a break from ciphers to earn [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]], though he also said he wouldn't be against [[Chandrilan cocktail]], Master Codebreaker paid a visit to the [[Brentaal Trading Houses]] on [[Brentaal IV]], one of the few [[Planet|worlds]] that still allow Codebreaker to play the games of odds which he recorded in the logbook.<ref name="Smuggler's Guide" />

After his sojourn on Brentaal and parts spinward, he continued trying to uncover the secrets of the logbook, and suggested that it could be [[bio-hexacrypt]]ed and that he only needed to determine the biological sample Maz selected for encryption to crack this. He was also reminded that regardless of which faction holds power, [[Galactic Republic]] or [[Galactic Empire]], [[New Republic]] or [[First Order]], business interests retain their grip on manufacturing. Eventually, Master Codebreaker managed to decode the meaning of the logbook, concluding that it is an elaborate cipher that Codebreaker claimed means "Happy [[Fete Week/Canon|Fete Week]]," wondering if it was an elaborate way by Maz to wish him [[New Year Fete Week|New Year Fete]]. He recorded his attempts to decode the ''Smuggler's Guide'' in it.<ref name="Smuggler's Guide" />

Later, Master Codebreaker tried to send the ''Smuggler's Guide'' back on course to [[Takodana]] as a thank you to Maz, so he decided to place it in the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]''. He managed to locate the<ref name="Smuggler's Guide" /> [[YT-1300 light freighter|YT-1300f light freighter]],<ref name="Cross">''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref> and sneak the logbook on board, thinking [[Han Solo]] wouldn't notice it. The book then ended up being discovered by [[Gannis Ducain]].<ref name="Smuggler's Guide" />

===Rolling on Canto Bight===
[[File:Last-jedi-databank-master-codebreaker-cropped.png|thumb|The Master Codebreaker with his companions at the Casino.|left|239x239px]]
In [[34 ABY]],<ref name="Date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of {{Film|VIII}} to [[34 ABY]].</ref> shortly after the [[Hosnian Cataclysm]], the Master Codebreaker attended the [[Canto Casino and Racetrack|Canto Casino]] in [[Canto Bight]] on the [[planet]] [[Cantonica]] together with<ref name="Episode VIII" /> his two female companions [[Centada Ressad]] and a human woman who he nicknamed "[[Lovey]]" as she refused to give him her real name.<ref name="Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: The Last Jedi: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> At the same time, the [[Resistance]] members [[Rose Tico]] and [[Finn]] [[Mission to Canto Bight|were sent]] to Cantonica by Kanata to hire the Master Codebreaker to stop the [[First Order]]'s [[flagship]], the ''[[Supremacy]]'', from [[Hyperspace tracker|tracking]] the Resistance's fleet through [[hyperspace]]. When they finally spotted him in the casino, they attempted to run up to him, but were apprehended by the [[Canto Bight Police Department]] for illegally parking their [[starship]] on the beach.<ref name="Episode VIII" /> "Lovey" then asked him about the disturbance, and he responded that he thought it was of little consequence.<ref name="Episode VIII" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|You'll find him with a red plom bloom on his lapel, rolling at a high stakes table in the casino on Canto Bight.|Maz Kanata|<ref name="Episode VIII" />}}
The "Master Codebreaker" was only known by his title, and kept his original identity a secret. However, he once posted all of his personal information to a public node, encrypted by [[bio-hexacrypt]], and anybody who uncovered the information was welcome to take his mantle. However, nobody was known to have retrieved the information.<ref name="Visual Dictionary" />

Matching his levels of secrecy, the Codebreaker's human companion kept her real name hidden from him as she intended to take his title from him and as such he only referred to her as "Lovey". At the Canto Casino, Master Codebreaker was only allowed to play dice games, and he was forbidden from electronic entertainment.<ref name="Visual Dictionary" /> He regularly wore a brooch in the shape of a red [[flower]], a [[plom bloom]], pinned on his lapel, which Maz told Finn and Rose about as an identifying mark. On the day he was sought out by the pair, he was sporting a thin black mustache.<ref name="Episode VIII" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Master Codebreaker is a character created by [[Rian Johnson]] for the [[2017]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VIII ''The Last Jedi'']]. He was portrayed by [[Justin Theroux]], who was cast one day before filming.<ref name="Art TLJ">''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Last Jedi]]''</ref>

In earlier versions of the film's script, Finn and Rose met the Master Codebreaker inside a cabaret room of the [[Canto Casino and Racetrack|Canto Casino]]. The Codebreaker enlists their help to steal jewels from an insectoid warlord known as the [[Butcher of Brix]]. The three climb onto the [[casino]]'s rooftop intending to break into the warlord's room, but are spotted by a surveillance [[droid]]. The Codebreaker is abducted using a "taser beam" from a huge prison ship, and Finn and Rose are arrested by the [[Canto Bight Police Department]].<ref name="Art TLJ" /> [[Jason Fry]], the author of the film's [[Star Wars: The Last Jedi: Expanded Edition|novelization]], originally wanted (along with Johnson) to include this alternate meeting between the Codebreaker, Finn and Rose to shake up the fans' expectations, but ultimately it was decided that presenting an alternate version of a major scene would shake up expectations too much, so the idea was dropped.<ref name="Independent">{{WebCite|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/books/features/star-wars-last-jedi-book-expanded-edition-author-jason-fry-interview-luke-skywalker-han-solo-rian-a8245706.html|text=Star Wars: The Last Jedi: Expanded Edition author on creating new scenes, reimagining Luke Skywalker's life, and working with Rian Johnson|author=Sheperd, Jack|date=2018-03-11|work=[[Wikipedia:The Independent|''The Independent'']]|archivedate=20200819025732}}</ref>
